inputs.text: Health workers from the Joint Health Sector Unions and the Assembly of Healthcare Professional Associations protested at Unity Fountain in Maitama, Abuja, on Thursday because reform bills are being advanced without the people who keep healthcare functioning. That’s a serious failure of democratic accountability: sidelining frontline workers means ignoring both their expertise and the realities patients face. When reforms are made over workers’ heads, people already facing unequal access to care are most likely to pay the price. Lawmakers should put workers, patients, and public health at the center—not deepen inequality through decisions made without them.
